chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by homiletic/application material: a sun-ray analogy is immediately applied to Mani’s own person, the Elect, love/charity, and salvation from the dark universe. There is no sustained, impersonal, system-internal cosmological mapping (degree-structures, body–cosmos correspondences, or systematic mechanics) that would signal the pre-compilation teaching substrate. The opening is a clear hagiographic frame formula.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative setup (“Once again… disciples… congregation”) typical of the Kephalaia’s editorial/hagiographic container, not the teaching substrate.

Imperative homiletic prompt (“Note how…”) introducing an illustrative analogy. Though it describes a cosmic object (sun/rays), it functions as sermon illustration rather than systematic cosmos→cosmos exposition; it prepares an application to the community/teacher in the next paragraph.

First-person self-application (“this is also what I am like!”), plus institutional/community identifiers (“my children… righteous elect… in every country”) and promissory gathering-soteriology. This is application voice anchoring the analogy to Mani and the Elect rather than an older impersonal cosmological teaching.
Direct exhortation to the audience (“I say to you… let him love…”) with Elect/charity language and salvation outcome—characteristic institutional-pastoral material, not substrate cosmology.
